findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys used by audit logs
findings.body:
`get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so this raises `TypeError` on a datetime for any non-empty page.

`value_from_cursor` has a matching problem: it returns the raw integer cursor value, which `build_queryset` then compares against a timestamp column (`datetime <= 1700000000000`). That comparison is a type error at the database level.

Every request with `optimized_pagination=true` will therefore return a 500. The class should reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key and value conversion.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises, and the intent is unsafe
findings.body:
The 'advanced' branch passes `cursor.offset < 0` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with `ValueError`/`AssertionError`, so any client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` crashes the request with a 500.

The stated purpose, "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", is not a legitimate feature either. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

findings.title: BasePaginator forwards negative offsets for prev cursors to the queryset
findings.body:
`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps offsets only for next cursors. A user-crafted prev cursor with a negative offset (`Cursor.from_string` accepts it) is passed to `queryset[...]`, which raises a ValueError and produces a 500.

The later check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` also still uses the unclamped `offset`. This change touches every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` user. Negative offsets should be rejected uniformly.

findings.title: Wrong authorization check for 'admin-only' paginator
findings.body:
The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` rather than an active-superuser check such as `is_active_superuser(request)`. A user with the superuser flag but no active superuser session passes.

The other half of the gate is `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. That flag is true for any member of an org with open membership, not only administrators.

In addition, `organization_context.member` can be None (for example, staff or non-member access). In that case the attribute access raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

findings.title: Switching span buffer keys from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight data on deploy
findings.body:
Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys in Redis are SETs written by the old code. After deploy, several operations hit those keys:
- `zadd` here
- `zcard`/`zunionstore` in `add-buffer.lua`
- `zscan` in `_load_segment_data`

All of these fail with WRONGTYPE errors against SET keys. The consumer and flusher will crash or loop until those keys expire, which can take up to `redis_ttl`, i.e. one hour.

A migration path is needed: new key prefix, a type check, or draining before rollout.

findings.title: Silent hardcoded eviction replaces configurable span-count limit
findings.body:
The script hardcodes a limit of 1000 and silently `zpopmin`s the excess spans, with no metric and no log.

Meanwhile `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is now unused, and the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and log were removed. The configuration is dead and inconsistent with the actual limit, and data loss is unobservable.

A related problem: `zunionstore` uses the default SUM aggregation, so a payload present in both sets gets a doubled score. That distorts which spans are evicted. The limit should be passed as an ARGV and the eviction counted in a metric.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x without justification
findings.body: The redirect-following loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining its consequence was removed. Segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now be split into separate segments instead of joined correctly.

findings.title: No tests for eviction or the new paginator
findings.body:
The PR's headline behavior has no tests:
- trimming segments over 1000 spans via `zpopmin`, and which spans survive
- `OptimizedCursorPaginator`
- the new audit-log branch

A basic test of the paginator would have revealed its datetime and negative-offset crashes.
